boundary_cells.statement: E<E_c(ell) has no real radial motion
E=E_c has J_r=0 and a closed circular orbit, or the center equilibrium when ell=0
E=0 is marginal escape and T_r,J_r diverge
noncentral bound trajectories cross the smooth center and their full Cartesian period is 2T_r
the displayed positive ratio uses L>=0; negative L reverses its sign while ell=abs(L) controls the geometry
b to zero at fixed ell>0 gives ratio one; ell=0 reaches the Kepler collision singularity and is not a smooth commuting corner

model.parameters: mu>0, b>0, signed angular momentum L; ell=abs(L)
model.phase_space: planar central motion; polar chart for ell>0 and Cartesian continuation for ell=0
model.radial_action_convention: J_r=(1/pi) integral from periapsis to apoapsis; at ell=0 use the continuous half-line limit

nonclaims: the isochrone potential, its action formula, and its frequency map are classical and are not claimed as literature originality
finite algebraic cells and numerical quadratures do not prove the all-parameter theorem
closed resonant tori are continuous families rather than isolated arithmetic primitive owners
the natural Schroedinger quantization is not identified with a target Hilbert-Polya operator

proof_contract.action_integration: partial_E J_r=T_r/(2pi), with J_r=0 at the unique circular energy
proof_contract.apsidal_integral: partial fractions of (x-b)/(x(x-2b)) and both root products give Delta_phi=pi(1+ell/sqrt(ell^2+4mu b))
proof_contract.closure_logic: return of the nonconstant radial phase forces an integer number of radial cycles; angular return is then equivalent to rational frequency ratio
proof_contract.finite_role: finite algebraic cells and quadrature controls are regression evidence only, not the all-parameter proof
proof_contract.period_integral: the root sum and the arcsine integral give the exact angular-momentum-independent radial period
proof_contract.substitution: x=b+sqrt(b^2+r^2), so r^2=x(x-2b) and dt=(x-b) dx/sqrt(Q(x))

references.title: L'amas isochrone II: Le calcul des orbites

references.ownership: official appendix recording the isochrone frequency map
references.title: Linear response theory and damped modes of stellar clusters
references.venue: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society 509 (2022), 2443-2456

theorem_contract.closure: a noncircular bound orbit with ell>0 is phase-space periodic iff the frequency ratio is rational
theorem_contract.degenerate_boundaries: circular orbits are closed independently of the ratio; ell=0 noncentral bound motions cross the smooth center and return after 2 T_r
theorem_contract.energy_domain: bound motion exists exactly for E_c(ell)<=E<0, where E_c=-2 mu^2/(ell+sqrt(ell^2+4 mu b))^2
theorem_contract.escape: E=0 is the marginal escape threshold and E>0 is unbound; J_r and T_r diverge as E increases to zero
theorem_contract.frequency_ratio: for ell>0, Omega_phi/Omega_r=(1+ell/sqrt(ell^2+4 mu b))/2; this is the L>=0 convention
theorem_contract.kepler_limit: for fixed ell>0, b decreases to zero gives J_r=mu/sqrt(-2E)-ell and frequency ratio one
theorem_contract.period: T_r=2 pi mu/(-2E)^(3/2), independent of ell
